title: Llevar + gerund: how long something had been going on

sections.content: You know *seguir* + gerund and *empezar a* from A2 Unit 28. *Llevar* + a time expression + gerund is another one: it says how long something has been going on, or, with the imperfect, how long it had been going on at a moment in the past. Use it to describe Mexico before 1910.

items.spanish: En 1910, Díaz llevaba más de treinta años gobernando.
items.english: In 1910 Díaz had been governing for more than thirty years.

items.spanish: México llevaba décadas recibiendo inversión extranjera.
items.english: Mexico had been receiving foreign investment for decades.

items.spanish: Muchos campesinos llevaban años pidiendo tierras.
items.english: Many peasants had been asking for land for years.

items.spanish: Mi vecina lleva tres años estudiando historia.
items.english: My neighbour has been studying history for three years.

sections.content: *Llevar* changes with the subject and the time: *Díaz llevaba*, *los campesinos llevaban*, *mi vecina lleva*. The gerund never changes. Use the imperfect for "had been" and the present for "has been".
